A section cut A-A was added. Verified in the payload rather than inferred from the worksheet's 'A 2 -> 4' count row: the reference's only two A texts are margin grid labels at the sheet edges (1028.6, 679.3) and (45.9, 679.3) on layer WAKU; the revision carries those same two re-traced onto the frame layer PLUS two more at (262.0, 219.0) and (262.0, 81.7) on NoLayerName_001, vertically aligned - a cut plane with a label at each end. Those two (REV-11D, REV-11F) plus the cut line and its ticks are part of THIS finding, not separate ones. The view being cut already exists on both sides. is_bulk true: designation + 2 end labels + cut line + arrow ticks exceeds the 5-entity convention. WARNING - this is a deliberate known false negative: DROP_SECTION_CALLOUT_LABELS has been True since cache v38 and the gotcha 'The Engine Ignored the Section Callout but the Canvas Still Drew It' argues the engine is right to drop the letters. Labelled anyway because a newly indicated section cut is a real drawing change even when the letter naming it is arbitrary. Owner-confirmed 2026-08-17.

An isometric view was added, and NOTHING in the worksheet's text diff can show it - it carries no text at all. Measured against the pinned aspect-1.414 iso zone: the reference's iso box (x 805-975, y 458-631) holds 0 entities; the revision's (x 322-390, y 183-252) holds 43 - 38 ellipse, 4 line, 1 block - of which 0 are text or dimension. 13 concentric ellipses (major axis 12-26) centred at (365.6, 224.0) plus 25 small ones, a circular feature in projection. Because COMPARABLE_ENTITY_TYPES is ('text', 'dimension'), the engine cannot report this under any tuning: it is a structural false negative, and it corroborates the ledger's own negative result that isometric_view has no coverage because the correct iso box holds zero comparable entities - here on a human pair rather than a mutation. Anchored by anchor rule 3 (lowest payload index, REV#526 = the first ellipse); rules 1 and 2 are unavailable because there is no callout and no text. is_bulk true at 43 entities.
